sentences.text:
Date : 17.11.2025 Heard Mr. A.R. Bhuyan, learned counsel for the petitioner; Ms. M. Barman,
learned Junior Government Advocate, Assam for the respondent nos. 1, 3, 5, 6 & 8; and Mr. J.K.
Goswami, learned Standing Counsel, Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Department for the respondent nos. 2, 4 & 7.

2 . The petitioner has stated that he is running a restaurant by the name and style of 'Shahi Biryani Hotel' after obtaining a valid license under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 from the Commissionerate of Food Safety [Health & Family Welfare Department], Government of Assam,
which is valid up-to 20.10.2026.

entities.text: Commissionerate of Food Safety [Health & Family Welfare Department], Government of Assam
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner has also obtained permission and trade license from Nilbagan Gaon Panchayat to run the restaurant as per the provisions of the Assam Panchayat Raj Act, 1986.
Page No.# 3/4 3.

The petitioner is aggrieved by an Order dated 26.09.2025 passed by the District Magistrate, Hojai [the respondent no. 5] purportedly in exercise of the powers under Section 152 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita [BNSS], 2023.

The assail is made to the impugned Order on the ground Md. Fakrul Islam vs The State Of Assam And 7 Ors on 17 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150603544/
2

entities.text: Md. Fakrul Islam vs The State Of Assam And 7 Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that by issuing the impugned Order dated 26.09.2025, the respondent no. 5 has illegally closed the restaurant of the petitioner, which is the only means of livelihood of the petitioner.
It is submitted that the respondent no. 5 without any enquiry, recorded findings in the impugned Order which are evidently perverse.
There is no element of public nuisance and the order has been passed beyond authority and jurisdiction of the respondent no. 5.

4. Per contra, the learned State Counsel has submitted that the impugned Order is an order of interim nature as the petitioner has the option to show cause against the Order under Section 154,
BNSS and the respondent no. 5 after going through the cause shown can either drop the proceeding or can modify or make the order absolute under Section 157, BNSS.
The petitioner has not availed such opportunity in the instance case.
5. The matter would require consideration.

6. Issue notice, returnable on 15.12.2025.
7.

As Ms. Barman, learned Junior Government Advocate, Assam has appeared and accepted notice on behalf of the respondent nos. 1, 3, 5, 6 & 8; and Mr. Goswami, learned Standing Counsel, Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Department has appeared and accepted notice on behalf of the respondent nos. 2, 4 & 7, issuance of formal notice to the said respondents is dispensed with.
However, extra copies of the writ petition along with annexures are to be Page No.# 4/4 furnished to Ms. Barman and Mr. Goswami within 2 [two] working days from today.

8. The learned State Counsel shall obtain the relevant records leading to passing of the impugned Order dated 26.09.2025 to place the same before the Court on the returnable date.
9. On the basis of the records placed and the counter affidavit filed, an endeavour will be made to give consideration to the writ petition.
JUDGE Comparing Assistant Md. Fakrul Islam vs The State Of Assam And 7 Ors on 17 November, 2025
